A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same UDBM research work, with complete main text and Appendices A–J. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 3–35 are identical; the changes on pages 1–2 are fully readable.

before.justification: v1 reports original UDBM restoration experiments in Tables 1–6, plus trajectory validation, inference-step experiments, and uncertainty-guidance robustness analyses in Appendices F and J.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative and qualitative results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The relaxed diffusion bridge, uncertainty-guided path and noise schedules, estimator, training objective, and inference procedures are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices G–I.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five-task AiO restoration coverage, task-specific denoising and deblurring, real-world datasets, and unseen CDD11 composite degradations. Section 4 and Appendix I.3 are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding comparison, including the task-specific baselines, AiO methods such as DiffUIR and HOGformer, and the DiffUIR trajectory comparison in Appendix F.4.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, preprocessing, model configurations, training budgets, evaluation metrics, and inference-step protocols are identical in Section 4 and Appendices I–J.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component and estimator ablations, schedule sensitivity, manifold alignment, trajectory validation, inference-step studies, and uncertainty-guidance robustness tests (Table 6, Figures 5–8, Appendices F and J).

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the benchmark results; the model's uncertainty estimation is also unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains UDBM-L's average 32.61 dB PSNR and 0.933 SSIM, while appendix Table 11 retains CDD11 LIQE values of 2.898 at one step and 2.931 at eight steps.

T1.justification: The assumptions, propositions, theorems, equations, and derivations in Section 3 and Appendices A–F are identical, including the drift-regularization and single-step inference arguments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and claims about uncertainty-guided transport, resolving drift singularity, and state-of-the-art single-step restoration. The new code statement does not revise those claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including the explanation of additional-step benefits under distribution shift in Appendix J.1 and failures under severe estimator-input noise or excessive uncertainty scaling in Appendix J.2.

D1.justification: v2's abstract adds a code-availability statement and a link to the Jabruson/UDBM repository. v1 only promises code and data upon acceptance on page 13; that promise remains in v2. This adds access information, while implementation details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not verify repository contents.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to diffusion bridges, prompt-based restoration, and mixture-of-experts methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds one code-availability sentence to the abstract and updates the preprint date and arXiv version text. The remaining wording, terminology, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer abstract causes limited text reflow between columns and pages 1–2, with altered paragraph spacing. All figures and tables retain their contents, captions, and designs; pages 3–35 have identical rendered layouts.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer provides a modest practical improvement over v1's release-upon-acceptance promise by making the stated code location discoverable. Scientific content and evidence are unchanged. The unrevised future-release statement on page 13 leaves release status unclear, so the benefit is limited to access documentation rather than verified reproducibility.
